A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from OmniReason to CogDriver. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial rewriting.

before.justification: V1 reports original planning and VQA results, component and temporal-memory ablations, and an OmniDrive evaluation in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: V2 retains those original evaluations and additionally reports Bench2Drive closed-loop results, inference throughput, and temporal-coherence examples.

M1.justification: V2 presents MVST-MLLM, multiview aggregation, and Future History Alignment as annotation innovations, whereas v1 names Qwen2.5-VL-72B. However, v2 retains a Qwen decoder and the same multiview, five-frame, ground-truth-conditioned workflow without clearly distinguishing modifications from newly documented internals. The agent's temporal-memory operations and training losses otherwise match.

E1.justification: V2 actually evaluates interactive closed-loop driving on Bench2Drive, extending beyond v1's reported open-loop planning and VQA evaluations. V1 mentions closed-loop tasks but provides no corresponding results. The nuScenes, Bench2Drive VQA, and OmniDrive coverage is retained; the dataset renaming alone adds no coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 introduces comparisons with AD-MLP, UniAD-Tiny/Base, TCP, ThinkTwice, DriveAdapter, MomAD, DriveTransformer, ReAL-AD, CogAD, and VAD. ORION is removed from the retained nuScenes comparison. Qwen2.5VL 32B and Omni-Q also appear in new throughput and qualitative comparisons, respectively; the VQA comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added Bench2Drive evaluation introduces closed-loop Driving Score, Success Rate, Efficiency, and Comfortness measurements. A separate throughput protocol uses one NVIDIA A800, 256 × 256 images, and 300 tokens. The retained nuScenes prediction horizons, VQA metrics, batch size, and stated learning rates are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds focused throughput analysis and frame-by-frame decision/rationale case studies, including an Omni-Q comparison in Figure 17. Its new Figure 4 replaces v1's single-scene VQA illustration. The numerical component and memory ablations, dataset-distribution analyses, and four appendix case examples are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's added evaluations do not introduce uncertainty estimation or statistical testing.

E6.justification: V2 adds Bench2Drive results of 78.21 Driving Score and 56.93% Success Rate, plus throughput of 3410.81 input and 391.43 output tokens/s. It also adds qualitative coherence findings and removes ORION's result entries. The retained nuScenes scores, VQA tables, numerical ablations, and OmniDrive results are unchanged; the new evaluations are not between-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Algorithm 1 reorganizes the temporal propagation, normalization, and attention operations already described by v1's equations and diagram. The training losses remain equivalent. No substantive theoretical result, proof, or formal definition of cognitive inertia is added.

C1.justification: V2 shifts the central contribution from interpretable spatiotemporal reasoning toward cognitive inertia, persistent intentions, stable internal representations, and reduced decision jitter. It claims the first benchmark for cognitively coherent agents and adds headline closed-loop and L2 improvement percentages. These substantially broaden the claimed capabilities despite unchanged retained planning scores.

C2.justification: V2 interprets closed-loop success and evolving framewise rationales as evidence of persistent intent and coherent internal world representations. It also interprets token throughput as confirming real-time driving suitability. V1 mainly linked temporal memory to sequential reasoning and safer predictions. These are substantive new mechanism and applicability arguments.

D1.justification: V2 adds detailed annotation and agent prompt templates, a two-stage training description, a project link, and inference hardware/settings. Conversely, it removes v1's disclosure of 128 NVIDIA H20 GPUs and 96GB memory per GPU. These materially change reproducibility documentation without establishing that retained experiments used different training procedures.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work around cognitive inertia and world models, adding corresponding references and closed-loop comparison works. It removes ORION and the object-centric temporal-modeling reference explicitly credited as inspiration in v1, while describing motion-aware normalization as novel. Related-work discussion and dataset feature comparisons are also revised.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of the method are rewritten around CogDriver and cognitive inertia. Sections are numbered and reorganized, evaluation details move into the supplement, and new training and prompt subsections expand the appendix. These changes substantially alter the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the annotation pipeline, replaces the memory diagram with pseudocode, converts the nuScenes results table into three plots, and adds closed-loop and throughput tables plus prompt and coherence figures. Table 1 replaces Traffic Flow with a Cognitive column. Existing appendix plots and examples are redistributed rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 adds valuable closed-loop validation, throughput measurements, and reproducibility details. However, it removes ORION, which tied v1's 0.34 m average L2, while strengthening superiority claims and claiming quantitatively reduced decision jitter without reporting a quantitative jitter evaluation. The actual annotator modifications also remain unclear. These gains in evidence and documentation coexist with weaker comparison completeness and claim calibration, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
